guarantees.claim: When rx_enable is 0, sreg_d, bit_cnt_d, baud_div_d, tick_baud_d are driven to 0 and idle_d to 1.
When rx_enable is 1 and tick_baud_x16 is 0, sreg_d, bit_cnt_d, baud_div_d, idle_d retain their prior values, and tick_baud_d is forced to 0.
When rx_enable is 1 and tick_baud_x16 is 1, baud_div_d increments by 1, and tick_baud_d is set to 1 on overflow (carry out of 4‑bit addition).

When rx_enable is 1, idle_q is high and rx falls low, the receiver enters start‑of‑frame state: baud_div_d set to 8, tick_baud_d cleared, bit_cnt_d set to 11 or 10 based on parity_enable, sreg_d cleared, idle_d cleared.

When rx_enable is 1, not idle, tick_baud_q=1 and bit_cnt_q equals the total bit count (11 or 10), if rx is high (invalid start bit at mid‑bit), the receiver aborts: idle_d set to 1, bit_cnt_d cleared; sreg_d unchanged.

When rx_enable is 1, not idle, tick_baud_q=1, and not in the glitch abort case, the shift register sreg_d takes rx and shifts left (sreg_d = {rx, sreg_q[10:1]}), bit_cnt_d decrements by 1, and idle_d is set to 1 when bit_cnt_q reaches 1.

assumptions.claim: tick_baud_x16 is a one‑cycle pulse occurring 16 times per bit period, and tick_baud_q is the registered version of the tick signal, synchronous to the UART clock.
assumptions.risk: Misaligned baud counter and tick_baud_q would cause bit sampling at wrong times, leading to data corruption.

assumptions.claim: rx_enable must be asserted before and held during the entire reception of a character; deassertion will reset the receiver state and discard any in‑progress byte.
assumptions.risk: Loss of data without error indication; controlling logic may not detect the abort.

assumptions.claim: After a falling edge on rx while idle, rx must remain low for at least half a bit period (until the middle of the start bit) to prevent glitch abort.
assumptions.risk: Receiver will abort and return to idle, potentially missing the character or falsely interpreting noise.

uncertain_points.claim: If tick_baud_x16 and the start condition (idle_q && !rx) are true in the same cycle, baud_div_d is assigned 8, overwriting the tick‑based increment. This may skip a baud tick or offset the start bit timing.
uncertain_points.cond: coincidence of tick_baud_x16 and rx falling edge
uncertain_points.risk: Start bit sampling may be offset, leading to framing errors or data corruption.

uncertain_points.claim: The relationship between tick_baud_d and tick_baud_q is not shown here; it is assumed that tick_baud_d feeds a flop to produce tick_baud_q. Need to confirm that tick_baud_q is exactly tick_baud_d delayed by one cycle without glitches, and that no combinatorial loop exists.
uncertain_points.risk: If feedback is incorrect, tick_baud_q may be misaligned with baud counts.

uncertain_points.claim: Glitch detection only occurs at the middle of the start bit. If rx noise causes a transition after that but before the first data bit, the receiver may sample corrupt data without abort.
uncertain_points.risk: Corrupt data may be accepted as a valid byte.
